existing_exercise_inventory.method: Parsed native summary titles across live pages; inspected certified Easy/Medium/Hard labels separately; read relevant current C–E models and review evidence.

primer-probability.title: Sensor decisions, calibration and batch reliability
case_assumptions: Incoming fault probability and detector conditional rates are specified, not estimated.
Inspection perfectly removes faults at a fixed stated cost.
Calibration observes one fixed offset with independent Gaussian noises conditional on that offset.
Batch independence is invoked only for the exact product calculation.
primer-probability.content_difference_from_existing_drills: Joins conditional probability with optimal conditional loss; transfers calibration to predictive error, shared-offset averaging and a batch-level design requirement.
central_decisions: Inspect on alarm under the original base rate.
Use posterior mean offset correction; distinguish offset tolerance from reading tolerance.
Reduce per-package escape probability to meet a batch requirement.

book-c-example-alarm.optimal_rule: inspect on alarm; release on quiet

primer-systems.title: Held-input temperature control and delayed robot braking
case_assumptions: The thermal model is scalar, exact in the stated interval, with exact sensing and constant surroundings.
Inputs are held for five minutes; the continuously updated controller is a different system.
Robot speed is constant during delay; full braking stops at zero speed and then holds.
A stopping-distance boundary with zero final clearance is allowed.
The disturbed-temperature exercise assumes a sampled disturbance bound only.
primer-systems.content_difference_from_existing_drills: Derives a dimensional continuous model through its exact held-input update, actuator-compatible region and between-reading trajectory; transfers to braking latency, interval sensing and clipped feedback.
central_decisions: The specified gain preserves the temperature interval and converges under the nominal model.
A 0.4-second braking delay is too long for the stated initial state.
The disturbance and actuator requirements jointly determine a feasible gain interval.

primer-rl-nn.title: Production policies with maintenance budgets and robust learned nominations
case_assumptions: The ready/worn state is observed and Markov; transition probabilities are fixed.
The policy draws fresh actions at each ready shift and discount is 0.8.
The claimed optimum is over the stated one-parameter policy family.
Learned mode selection happens once before an episode; each selected mode then keeps its fixed policy parameter.
The transition model applies independently of the initial reading.
Robustness uses hard sensor-error bounds for a fixed specified network.
primer-rl-nn.content_difference_from_existing_drills: Uses action-dependent wear to calculate delayed maintenance, optimise a constrained policy family, and gate a robust but infeasible neural nomination; transfers to uncertain wear, fixed bias and long-run operational rates.
central_decisions: Choose p=5/9 under the original expected discounted budget.
Reject the robust nomination of mode B and choose feasible fallback A.
Reduce the policy probability when the wear probability has a hard uncertainty interval.

word_count_method: HTMLParser text content plus regex word tokens; word_count includes mathematical tokens, prose_word_count_excluding_math removes all inline and display math.

numerical_methods: Enumerate all fault/alarm outcomes and every deterministic sensor rule.
Condition the joint Gaussian through its measurement covariance, independently of precision addition.
Sum all reading-error covariances to check the shared-offset variance floor.
Sum a binomial tail to check the independent batch probability.
Integrate held-input thermal dynamics with RK4 independently of the exact sampled formula.
Integrate linear braking speeds and check stopping margins along trajectories.
Check extremal corners and affine-piece endpoints of invariant-set calculations.
Solve reward and cost Bellman systems directly and compare with 1000-step exact forward probability propagation.
Propagate the state distribution to its stationary law and check operational rates.
Evaluate ReLU score pieces, slopes, boundary ties and allowed perturbations.

claim_review: Every numerical case is explicitly hypothetical; no empirical or citation claims were introduced.
The cost-optimal sensor rule is not described as preventing every fault.
Offset and predictive reading probabilities are distinguished; shared uncertainty is not averaged away.
Posterior probabilities are not presented as frequentist confidence bounds or hard finite error bounds.
Sampled thermal stability, actuator limits, sampled invariance and between-reading behaviour are separately justified.
Robot delay and interval uncertainty are included before stating stopping feasibility.
Expected discounted maintenance, individual episodes and stationary operating rates remain distinct.
A fixed-network input certificate is explicitly separated from policy-budget feasibility.
The material does not alter or claim expansion of existing Lean proof coverage.
limitations: All physical and stochastic models are teaching assumptions; no empirical validation is claimed.
Numerical recomputation supports arithmetic and examples; it is not a formal proof of the general arguments.
A hard parameter or measurement interval is only useful if it contains the real quantity; confidence in estimated intervals is outside these cases.
Final integrated browser validation belongs to root because this agent writes fragments only.

independent_peer_review.finding: C.B2 needed an explicit zero-mean Gaussian fresh-noise law; variance alone cannot determine the quoted probability.
